abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework termed Socio-Cognitive Requirements Engineering (SCRE), which fundamentally reconceptualizes requirements elicitation as a collaborative sense-making process rather than a traditional information extraction activity. Unlike conventional approaches that treat stakeholders as passive information providers, SCRE positions requirements engineering within the broader context of organizational knowledge construction, drawing upon distributed cognition theory and activity theory. The framework proposes three foundational principles: (1) requirements emerge through negotiated interpretation rather than simple communication, (2) stakeholder cognitive models are inherently distributed and dynamically evolving, and (3) the elicitation process itself transforms both the problem space and the solution space. We demonstrate how this paradigmatic shift enables requirements engineers to handle ambiguity, contradiction, and change more effectively by treating these phenomena as inherent characteristics rather than obstacles. The theoretical contributions include a formal model of stakeholder cognition during requirements activities, a typology of sense-making patterns observed in elicitation sessions, and a set of evaluative criteria for assessing requirements quality from the socio-cognitive perspective. This framework opens new research directions in requirements elicitation, particularly concerning how digital tools can support rather than impede natural human sense-making processes.

Goal-oriented requirements modeling has long relied on strategic rational analysis for deriving system requirements from stakeholder goals. This paper presents an enhanced theoretical foundation for goal modeling that integrates emotional and motivational dimensions previously underrepresented in formal approaches. Building upon the KAOS methodology and its linguistic foundations, we introduce the Conceptually Enhanced Goal Model (CEGM) that extends traditional goal decompositions with affective annotations and motivational classifications. The theoretical contribution lies in establishing formal connections between goal types (achieve, maintain, avoid) and stakeholder emotional states (satisfaction, concern, anxiety), enabling more comprehensive requirements analysis. We define a set of transformation rules that propagate emotional considerations through goal hierarchies, ensuring that derived requirements preserve both rational and affective requirements. The paper also proposes evaluation criteria for assessing the emotional coherence of goal models and presents a reasoning mechanism for detecting potential conflicts arising from incompatible stakeholder motivations. Case studies from the healthcare domain demonstrate that CEGM identifies requirements that would be missed by purely rational analysis, particularly concerning user acceptance and system adoption factors. This work contributes to bridging the gap between formal requirements specification and the psychological reality of stakeholder decision-making.

This paper presents TRACE-IA, a novel requirements traceability system that fundamentally transforms how traceability relationships are established and maintained throughout the software development lifecycle. Unlike traditional traceability tools that rely on manual link creation or simplistic keyword matching, TRACE-IA employs a hybrid architecture combining large language models with structured ontology reasoning to generate, validate, and manage bidirectional traceability links between requirements, design artifacts, and test cases. The system introduces three innovative capabilities: (1) semantic traceability generation using contextual embeddings that understand natural language descriptions beyond keyword overlap, (2) dynamic traceability maintenance that automatically propagates changes through the artifact graph when requirements evolve, and (3) uncertainty-aware traceability that explicitly represents confidence levels and explains reasoning behind generated links. The architecture leverages a purpose-built requirements knowledge graph that captures domain-specific semantics while remaining adaptable across application domains. An extensive evaluation involving industrial practitioners demonstrates that TRACE-IA achieves 87% precision and 82% recall on traceability link generation, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art approaches. The system has been deployed in three software development organizations, showing measurable improvements in impact analysis efficiency and requirements validation completeness.

User story quality significantly impacts agile software development success, yet existing story writing tools lack sophisticated support for quality assessment and refinement. This paper presents StoryForge, an intelligent environment that enhances the user story development process through automated quality analysis and guided refinement. Building upon the INVEST framework, StoryForge implements a multi-dimensional quality model that evaluates stories along independence, negotiability, value, estimation accuracy, smallness, and testability dimensions. The system architecture comprises three integrated components: a natural language parser that extracts structural elements from story descriptions, a quality analyzer that applies rule-based and machine learning techniques to assess each dimension, and a refactoring engine that generates actionable suggestions for improvement. Unlike prior approaches that provide only binary quality indicators, StoryForge generates detailed diagnostic reports explaining specific weaknesses and proposing concrete reformulations. The paper describes the iterative refinement process enabled by the tool, where authors can progressively improve stories while maintaining consistency with the broader product backlog. An empirical study with 24 agile teams demonstrates that stories refined using StoryForge exhibit 34% higher acceptance rates and 28% fewer defects compared to baseline approaches, validating the practical value of enhanced story quality support.
